extracted.intended_audience: general readers researching Reddit (including PR/marketing and communications professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical principles for brands, PR teams, and communicators planning to post, run AMAs, or otherwise engage with Reddit communities; emphasizes listening, authenticity, topic-focused participation, and appropriate use of community managers or subreddits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen first / don't exploit communities
rubrics_metrics.description: The communities on Reddit don't want to feel used or exploited. That's where listening comes in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before posting or launching campaigns, learn the community; listen to norms and conversations rather than immediately pushing promotional material. Several cited sources (e.g., 'To Learn About reddit, Listen First') stress that listening prevents communities from feeling exploited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build credibility rather than chase virality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The point of posting to reddit is not to have content go viral; it is to build credibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame contributions to establish long-term credibility and trust with redditors instead of designing posts solely to go viral. Content should add value to the community discussion rather than just seek attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the topic, not the brand
rubrics_metrics.description: 'On Reddit, Unlike Other Social Sites, It's About the Topic, Not the Brand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brands are discussed in a casual, community-driven context (compared to a local bar or coffee shop rather than a mall). Communications should emphasize useful, topical contribution over overt brand promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be authentic, transparent, and accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Users demand authenticity, transparency, and accountability; Reddit and its communities respond poorly to anything that seems inauthentic or deceptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging (e.g., AMAs or sponsored posts), be upfront about identity/intent, disclose sponsorships or brand ties, and accept community scrutiny. Reddit staff and moderators will call out or respond if content/presentations appear disingenuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage honestly and cleverly to win trust
rubrics_metrics.description: "Advertisers have to be willing to engage honestly — and cleverly — with the reddit community to win their trust."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to interact in real time, answer questions candidly, and craft messaging that respects community norms—creative, honest engagement is more effective than corporate-sounding messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use community managers to interact effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns that used dedicated community managers 'really responded well' (example: Nissan's reddit campaign responding positively to two community managers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ experienced community managers to organize interactions, verify participants (for AMAs), moderate responses, and steward the brand's presence within subreddit norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a subreddit's moderation doesn't suit you, create your own subreddit
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don't like how a moderator is managing a subreddit, the best solution is to start your own subreddit and moderate it with different rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than attempting to change another community's rules, launch and manage a branded or topic-focused subreddit with policies aligned to your goals and audience—but be prepared to maintain it in accordance with Reddit norms.
